newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romanian airline workers put off strike action.
newsitem.headline: Romanian airline workers put off strike action.

text.p: Workers at Romania's national airline Tarom said on Wednesday they were putting off a threat to go on strike and ground flights following new government proposals on restructuring the airline.

"We decided to postpone any protest until Monday when a cabinet meeting is supposed to discuss our problems and find a suitable solution," Sandu Panaite, a Tarom trade union leader, told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
He said ministers had promised to re-examine proposals by the State Ownership Fund (FPS), Romania's main privatisation agency, to cut wages and do away with 1,000 jobs.
But earlier in the day FPS boss Sorin Dimitriu told a news conference: "No sentimental reason or trade union action will be allowed in our restructuring plan."
Dimitriu said Tarom needed to cut jobs, withdraw ageing aircraft and improve efficiency after years of bad management.

Tarom's maintenance staff massed for the third consecutive day by hangars outside Bucharest's Otopeni airport. Flights have been unaffected, but staff have threatened to halt maintenance checks and shut down the airline's operations unless the plan is withdrawn.

Tarom has laboured in recent years under huge debts, compounded by high fees to air traffic control and airport authorities. Trade unions want state subsidies maintained and early retirement packages instead of layoffs. They have also asked the airline to shed loss-making subcontractors.

A restructuring plan to help the airline to compete in growing east European markets was initiated in 1995. But it stalled under leftists who had held power since the ousting of Communist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu in 1989 until their election defeat last year.
The carrier plans to buy eight new Boeing Co 737s as part of a project to upgrade its fleet.
